claim: In March 2026, J.P. Morgan began offering clients a basket of credit default swaps referencing five hyperscalers — Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle — a standardized way to hedge or speculate on the credit risk of the companies financing the AI build-out. Bloomberg reported the basket trades in $25 million increments, $5 million per name. The product followed a sharp widening in Oracle's credit-default-swap spreads, which traded around 126 basis points in late 2025 — described in the financial press as near the widest in years, with several outlets comparing it to levels last seen around the 2008 crisis — as Oracle's debt load passed $100 billion, largely to fund data-center capacity. The five hyperscalers issued roughly $121 billion of bonds in 2025, with analysts projecting up to $300 billion more in 2026.

sources.label: Bloomberg — “JPMorgan Offers Clients a New CDS Basket to Hedge AI Debt Risk,” March 23, 2026
Yahoo Finance — “Oracle Credit Default Swaps Surge as AI Debt Concerns Grow”
sources.quote: Oracle's CDS trade around 126 basis points, well above levels for other AI-linked companies such as Nvidia and Meta

notes: Companion to 2025-ai-datacenter-capex-001 on the same anchor — that record carries the capex-forecast scale; this one carries the credit market starting to price the tail risk (JPMorgan's CDS basket on the same five names, Oracle's CDS widening). The surfacing reel is an AI-generated Family Guy 'brain rot' explainer, but its factual spine checks out: the JPMorgan basket (Bloomberg, Mar 23 2026), the five named hyperscalers, the $25M/$5M trade increments, Oracle's ~126bp CDS and $100B+ debt are all reported. The directly-fetched Yahoo source said Oracle's CDS rose 'close to record levels'; the explicit 'highest since 2008' figure (~128bp, Dec 2025) appears in secondary reporting (ainvest, Voya, Fortune coverage) and the reel's '310%' is consistent with the move from ~30bp to ~126–128bp, but the precise '2008' superlative is attributed reporting, not asserted here. The reel's leap — that the swaps are 'doomsday tickets' presaging a systemic reset that turns 'your online life into an unsecured asset in bankruptcy court' — is dramatization, not in the sourcing.
